title: Sell Mineral Rights in Escambia County, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Escambia County, AL
metaDescription: Own mineral or royalty rights in Escambia County, Alabama, near the Jay Field Norphlet trend? Get a clear, patient cash offer on your interest.
heroLead: Escambia County sits at the heart of Alabama's most productive onshore oil and gas trend, home to a piece of the Jay Field discovery and decades of Smackover and Norphlet development that make it one of the most consistently active counties in the state for mineral ownership.
intro: If you hold a mineral or royalty interest in Escambia County, around Brewton, Flomaton, East Brewton, or the rural acreage between them, you are dealing with a genuinely active part of Alabama's oil and gas history, not a speculative fringe area. We evaluate these interests the way a family office looks at any real asset: understand the production, weigh the after-tax present value of holding against a lump sum today, and give you a straight answer either way.
This page walks through the geology, the courthouse realities, and what actually drives value here, so you know what to expect before you ever talk numbers with us.

sections.heading: The Smackover and Norphlet story in Escambia County
paragraphs: Escambia County sits within the broader south Alabama extension of the Jurassic Smackover trend, a carbonate formation that has produced oil across the Gulf Coast for nearly a century, capped in places by the Norphlet sandstone, a gas-condensate reservoir that became a major exploration target once operators understood how to find it. The Jay Field discovery in 1970, straddling the Alabama-Florida line, was one of the largest Norphlet finds ever made and triggered a wave of leasing across this entire corner of the state.

Much of that trend is structurally controlled by salt movement, with the Smackover and Norphlet draped over and around ancient salt features that created the traps operators drilled into. That geology means production in Escambia County tends to be concentrated in specific structural highs rather than spread evenly across the county, so two tracts a few miles apart can have very different production histories depending on their position relative to these features.

Decades into development, most of this county's wells are mature. Production has declined substantially from the field's peak years, but a meaningful number of wells continue producing at lower, stripper-well volumes, generating steady if modest royalty checks for the mineral owners tied to them.

sections.heading: Probate, heirs, and title work in Brewton
paragraphs: Brewton, the county seat, is where the Escambia County Probate Office holds deed, lease, and estate records for the entire county. Because heavy leasing activity in this area dates back to the early 1970s, a lot of the paperwork we deal with here is genuinely old, original lease agreements, early division orders, sometimes handwritten amendments, all of which we pull and review before quoting.

Heirs' property and tenancy-in-common situations are common in this county, the same as in most of rural south Alabama. A tract leased fifty years ago has often passed through two or three generations since, sometimes without formal probate at every step. We can usually work with a properly executed heirship affidavit to establish your ownership without requiring a full, drawn-out probate proceeding, though every family's situation is different and we will tell you honestly what yours requires.
We can also purchase from individual heirs separately when a family co-owns an undivided interest and not everyone wants to sell at the same time.

sections.heading: What actually moves the number on an Escambia County offer
paragraphs: Your net royalty decimal and recent production history matter most, but so does your tract's position relative to the historic Jay Field structure and any other locally productive units. An interest sitting within or near a well-documented producing area supports a stronger, more confident valuation than one on the trend's outer edge with a thinner history.

We also weigh the well's stage of decline. A stripper well late in its productive life behaves differently than one still on a steeper decline curve, and that shapes how we think about the present value of continuing to hold versus selling now. None of this is a fixed formula, it depends on your specific statements and current natural gas and condensate pricing, which is exactly why we ask to see your documentation before quoting a number rather than offering a blanket figure over the phone.

faqs.question: Is my Escambia County property actually part of the Jay Field trend?
faqs.answer: Some tracts are within the historical field boundary or its Alabama extension, and some sit outside it; we check your specific legal description against unit and production records to confirm.

faqs.question: Where are Escambia County's deed and probate records filed?
faqs.answer: At the Escambia County Probate Office in Brewton, the county seat, which holds records for the entire county including Flomaton and East Brewton.

faqs.question: My family's lease dates back to the early 1970s Jay Field boom. Is it still valid?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether production has continued to hold the lease; we research the current well status tied to your specific agreement before answering.

faqs.question: What if the estate that passed this interest to me was never formally probated?
faqs.answer: In many cases a signed heirship affidavit is enough to establish your ownership without full probate, though we review each situation individually to confirm what yours needs.

faqs.question: How does a mature, declining well affect what my interest is worth?
faqs.answer: A well later in its decline typically has a lower but more predictable remaining production stream, which we factor into a valuation based on recent statements rather than the field's historical peak output.

faqs.question: Should I get tax advice before selling a mineral interest here?
faqs.answer: It is worth understanding how a lump-sum sale compares to continued royalty income for your specific tax situation, and we encourage you to review that with your own CPA or tax advisor.
